resources.string: Open source components used in the app
Ogneliss has no internet permission. You can verify this yourself in the installed app details — your call log, contacts and notes stay on this device.
Why this dialer cannot record calls
This number is covered by the mask %1$s, not by a rule of its own. Unblocking it here would remove the mask and unblock the whole range with it. Open the block list to decide.
Numbers here always get through, whatever the other rules say. Add your clinic, school and courier here before turning on strict blocking.
The file contains notes, tags, block and allow lists and speed dial. Call history and contacts are not included — Android transfers those itself.
Cloud backup is disabled on purpose: your data does not leave the device. The flip side is that a new phone starts empty. Export keeps your notes, tags and block lists.
Couriers, clinics, schools and banks call from numbers that are not in your contacts. They will stop reaching you. Add exceptions to the allow list first.
The contact will be removed from every account it is stored in, including Google. This cannot be undone from the phone.
The incoming number will be passed to the app you choose, which may send it to its own servers.
All settings return to their defaults. Notes, tags and lists are kept.
Ogneliss needs access to the call log to show your history. It stays on the device.
Calls you make and receive will appear here.
Add someone to your phone book and they will appear here.
Without access to contacts, calls show as bare numbers and T9 search cannot find people by name.
Tap the star next to a contact to keep them at hand.
A note can be added from a contact card or right during a call. It stays on this phone.
Set one from a contact card or from the long-press menu in the call log.
Try fewer digits, or search by the first letters of a name.
Incoming numbers will be passed to %1$s. That app decides what to do with them under its own privacy policy.
No caller ID directories are installed on this device.
This is the only place where a number can leave your device. Not through Ogneliss — it has no network access — but through the app you enable here, which may send the number to its own servers.

Show incoming, outgoing and missed calls, group them and delete entries at your request. The log stays on this device.
Match names and photos to numbers, search contacts with T9, edit and star them. Contacts are never sent anywhere.
Show incoming calls in the shade with Answer and Decline buttons, plus call-back reminders.
Make and receive calls, detect the active SIM card. Without this the app cannot work as a dialer.

On — numbers you tagged as spam or fraud stop calling and appear as blocked in the log. Off — they still call, but the tag is shown in the log and on the call screen.
Use with care: couriers, clinics and schools call from unknown numbers. Add exceptions to the allow list.
Shared with Android. Blocked at the telephony level — the phone does not ring at all.

A notification with one-tap options: in 30 minutes, in 2 hours, this evening.
Repaints the app to match your wallpaper. Off by default so the app keeps its own colours.
Off by default. When enabled, the number is passed to the selected app.
Phone numbers and names in the log are masked. Useful when reporting a problem.
How repeated calls are combined in the list
Bigger keys and call buttons. Helpful with limited vision or dexterity.
The whole log as a CSV table: date, number, name, type, duration. Opens in Excel and LibreOffice.

Recommended: a popup after every call to family gets annoying fast.

On Android 10 and later the system blocks third-party apps from accessing call audio, and working around this is against Google Play policy. If your phone records calls, that feature is built in by the manufacturer and works regardless of which dialer you choose.

Put the phone down during a call and the speaker turns on. Pick it up and it switches back. Ignored with a headset or after you switch audio yourself.

Shown under the number, from the official numbering plan. For a mobile number this is the region where the number was issued, not where the caller is. Carrier and region come from the Russian registry; in other countries only the carrier is shown, and not for every number.

Android hands call control to one app at a time. Without this role Ogneliss cannot place or receive calls.
Without it the app will open, but nothing inside it will work.
You will not be able to make calls from the app, and it will not see which SIM is active.
The call list will stay empty and you will not see who called you.
Calls will show as bare numbers, and T9 search will not find people by name.
Incoming calls will not appear in the shade, and call-back reminders will not arrive.
Switching to the speaker or a Bluetooth headset during a call may not work.
Part of the app will not work.
See what is granted and fix what is missing
Use this if a permission dialog no longer appears — Android stops showing it after two refusals.
Ogneliss holds this role. Doubtful calls can be let through silently instead of being blocked.
Off by default: the app is opened more often to see who called than to dial.
A note about a delivery is useful for a week; a year later it is clutter. Notes tagged as spam or fraud are never deleted.
A note about someone in your contacts usually refers to a living relationship, not a one-off errand.
No calls does not mean no contact — you may be messaging these people daily.

Changes are saved automatically and apply to the call list right away.
How far the row must travel before the action fires. Lower is faster but fires by accident while scrolling.
The share of the distance after which the row snaps on its own. A low value feels uncontrollable during quick movements.
The speed at which a short flick is enough. A low value catches ordinary scrolling when your finger moves at a slight angle.
A vertical movement goes to the list immediately and the swipe does not intercept scrolling. Helps if your finger travels in an arc.
You can pin up to %1$d numbers. Pinned entries take the top of the screen — with more of them the call list would start below the visible area.
The call log could not be read. Check that access to the call log is granted in Settings.
Which numbers stay above the call list
Pinned numbers stay at the top of the call list regardless of when you last spoke. Useful while you are dealing with a courier, a repair or a one-off client — people you would not add to favourites.
You can also pin a number by holding an entry in the call list.

A small round button on the call log and contacts screens. Turn it off if you only need the menu, the launcher shortcut or the quick settings tile.
A number from your contacts. Left empty, a random contact is used.
The screen looks like an incoming call, but no call is made: nothing is sent anywhere and it does not appear in the call log. This is a way to step away from a conversation, not a safety tool.
Each call as a card, or calls grouped by day
